description: Two MAX485 RS-485 modules on one bus, driven by USART1 (node A, DE/RE on PA8) and USART3 (node B, DE/RE on PB12) of one Blue Pill: 3 rounds of PING / PONG with half-duplex direction control; report on USART2
expect:
72 MHz. Node A: USART1 PA9 -> MAX485 #1 DI, PA10 <- RO, PA8 -> DE+RE. Node B: USART3 PB10 -> MAX485 #2 DI, PB11 <- RO, PB12 -> DE+RE. Modules on 5 V, A-A and B-B joined, R7 (120 Ohm) fitted on both (the two bus ends). RO is 5 V, so both RX pins are 5 V tolerant (PA10, PB11). USART1/USART3 115200 8N1 (USART3 on PCLK1 36 MHz: BRR 19 + 8/16 = 115384.6 baud, +0.16 %, as on real silicon; USART2 likewise) with RXNE interrupts into 64-byte rings; DE/RE outputs low (receive) after init. USART2 PA2 115200 8N1 report: 'RS-485 ping-pong: A=USART1 (DE PA8) <-> B=USART3 (DE PB12), 115200 8N1
', then for i = 1..3: A raises DE, sends 'PING i
' (blocking, until TC), lowers DE; B waits up to 20 ms for the line and answers 'PONG i
' the same way; A waits up to 20 ms: 'round i: B got 'PING i', A got 'PONG i''. A missing line prints 'round i: B heard nothing' (or '..., A heard nothing'). Finally 'rs485 ok
' (all rounds matched) or 'rs485 FAILED
', then WFI. Without the modules (nothing on the bus) every round reports 'B heard nothing'.

circuit: MAX485 modules: not placed on this bench (the checks runner cannot place them; the ping-pong on a real two-module bus is covered by tests/devices/comm-firmware.test.ts)
USART2: virtual terminal on PA2 (TX) / PA3 (RX)

boot.USART2:
RS-485 ping-pong: A=USART1 (DE PA8) <-> B=USART3 (DE PB12), 115200 8N1
round 1: B heard nothing
round 2: B heard nothing
round 3: B heard nothing
rs485 FAILED
